title: Fidelity Lighthouse: automated calibration & accuracy sentinel for FP8/INT8 quant profiles
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: We need an automated, CI-friendly validation harness that verifies accuracy-preservation for new quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) across representative workloads before they reach production. Existing tools run ad-hoc calibrations and hand-curated golden checks; they are slow to run and hard to reproduce.

Goal: Build 'Fidelity Lighthouse' — a lightweight orchestrator + checker that: (1) runs calibration flows, (2) executes a curated set of anchor prompts (reference prompt cohort), (3) computes per-query and aggregate fidelity metrics with statistical confidence, and (4) emits pass/fail gates and triage artifacts (deltas, tox examples, representative traces). The harness must be runnable locally, in CI, and as a pre-release canary step in the runtime rollout pipeline.

Scope: validation for FP8 and INT8 quant profiles on decoder-only and encoder-decoder models used in Redwood's hosted catalog. This ticket covers design, core harness implementation, integration with the quant ci job, and the default anchor prompt set + metric thresholds. Integration with the Console alerts/rollout workflow will be tracked as a follow-up integration ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness (python runner + config) that runs calibration + validation end-to-end against a model artifact (container or model-id) and outputs a standardized result bundle (metrics.json, diffs.zip, example_fails.json)
Support for both FP8 and INT8 quant profiles via the runtime's quant CLI (profile name input) and ability to override calibration bins/context lengths
Default anchor prompt cohort of ~300 prompts covering NLU, summarization, instruction-following, math, and code; cohort can be extended by tests; prompts are tagged by domain
Aggregate fidelity metrics computed: exact-match rate (where applicable), top-k token agreement, edit-distance-normalized score, and a calibration-aware KL divergence for distributional outputs
A configurable pass/fail gate (JSON) with thresholds per-metric and a confidence level (95%) using bootstrap; harness fails CI when gate is breached
CI integration: job in quant-ci that runs on model-profile PRs and writes artifacts to test-results bucket with a stable path and GitHub PR comment summarizing results
Documentation (runbook + example invocation) in Confluence and a demo notebook in the repo
No nested JSONs in the result bundle root (flat keys) to keep downstream parsers simple
technical_notes: We will use bootstrap resampling for confidence intervals rather than parametric assumptions because distribution shapes vary across prompt types
Anchor prompts are intentionally short to keep token costs low for CI but include a small set of longer-context regression cases (max 2048 tokens)
Use continuous caching of KV prefixes between related prompt groups to approximate production runtime behavior during throughput-sensitive checks
Leverage existing quant calibration CLI (quant/cli:v2) for generating per-layer scale factors; harness orchestrates calls and validates outputs
For generation comparisons, use nucleus-sampling reruns to estimate stochastic variability; deterministic checks use fixed seeds
We will store diffs and traces in s3://redwood-quant-results/{run_id}/ and attach a summarized CSV for quick inspection
Pass/fail gate thresholds are conservative on first rollout; allow a grace buffer to reduce false positives while we tune anchor set
implementation_plan: Week 1: design finalization, finalize anchor prompt cohort and metric definitions; add ticket for anchor prompt curation owners
Week 2: scaffold harness repo and CLI, implement calibration orchestration and model invocation wrapper (supports local container or model-id)
Week 3: implement metrics modules (token agreement, EM where applicable, KL/divergence, edit-distance normalized score), bootstrap CI integration
Week 4: add result bundling, upload artifacts, GitHub PR comment plugin, and basic docs
Week 5: run experiments across 6 internal quant profiles, tune thresholds, and stabilize
Week 6: landing PRs, create quant-ci job, and demo to runtime/release owners
test_plan: Unit tests for metric functions with synthetic datasets (deterministic and stochastic cases)
Integration test that runs the harness against a small deterministic toy model (fast) in CI
End-to-end test that runs full anchor cohort on a sample FP8 profile nightly and asserts that the harness completes and produces expected keys
A/B comparison script to replay a previous 'golden' run and compute regressions over time
Manual review of top 25 failures per run by an ML engineer to classify failure modes (calibration error, tokenization mismatch, model change)
Load test: run harness with 10 parallel workers to validate resource limits and S3 throughput
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal integration — run on all quant profile PRs in internal CI; keep gate non-blocking but post results to PR
Stage 2: CI-blocking gate for dedicated-profile PRs after two weeks of stable signal and low false positives
Stage 3: Hook into canary rollout automation: if CI gate fails, prevent profile from being promoted to canary channels and notify runtime on-call
Stage 4: Add Console integration to surface per-profile regression trends (follow-up ticket)
metrics: primary_metric: token_agreement_rate (percent of tokens matching majority/reference) — pass threshold default 97%
confidence: 95% bootstrap CI for each metric; if CI lower bound breaches threshold, mark as fail
cost_budget: default harness run must complete under $10 for CI quick-check profile
